title: Short-acting beta 2 agonists (SABA) (salbutamol and terbutaline): reminder of the risks from overuse in asthma and to be aware of changes in the SABA prescribing guidelines
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 18, issue 9, April 2025: 1
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: Advises not to prescribe a short-acting beta2-agonist to people of any age with asthma without a concomitant inhaled corticosteroid, in line with NICE guideline NG245 (2024), and to review treatment of patients using 'as needed' SABA more than twice weekly. A review of SABA overuse was initiated in 2022 by the MHRA and by the EU PRAC; the evidence included observational data from 187,675 UK primary care records of patients aged 12 years and over (SABINA, Quint and others 2022), in which 3 or more SABA prescriptions over 1 year were associated with severe exacerbations independently of anti-inflammatory maintenance therapy, and UK product information was strengthened in 2023. A National Child Mortality Database report of December 2024 on child deaths from April 2019 to March 2023 identified 54 deaths due to asthma: 47 children (87%) had 3 or more reliever inhalers dispensed in the year before death and 27 (50%) 12 or more; 35 (65%) had fewer than 9 preventer inhalers dispensed and 23 (43%) 4 or fewer. Before December 2024, inhaled SABA alone was considered potentially sufficient for a small minority with infrequent, short-lived wheeze and normal lung function.
